rich_summary: Vasishtha’s divine cow Shabala defends her master against King Vishwamitra. Declaring that the spiritual power of a sage surpasses the might of a warrior, she asks permission to destroy the king’s pride. At Vasishtha’s command she miraculously generates armies—foreign soldiers and strange golden‑skinned warriors—who overwhelm Vishwamitra’s forces. Even when Vishwamitra counters with powerful weapons, Shabala produces more warriors from her own body, annihilating the king’s elephants, chariots, and troops. Vishwamitra’s hundred sons attack Vasishtha but are instantly burned to ashes when the sage utters a single sacred sound. Humiliated and stripped of glory, Vishwamitra abandons his kingdom and turns to severe asceticism. Winning the favor of Shiva, he gains divine knowledge and celestial weapons, setting the stage for a renewed confrontation with Vasishtha and marking the beginning of his transformation from king to spiritual seeker.

highlight_spans.why: Shabala declares the supremacy of a sage’s spiritual power over a warrior’s might, establishing the chapter’s core theme.
Shabala miraculously produces soldiers who begin destroying Vishwamitra’s army—one of the earliest displays of her supernatural power.
The strange golden-skinned warriors (Shakas) appear in vast numbers and consume the army like fire, escalating the battle into a mythic spectacle.
Warriors are born from Shabala’s body—feet, udders, hair, and thighs—showing the divine cow as a living source of limitless armies.
Vasishtha destroys Vishwamitra’s hundred sons with a single utterance, a dramatic moment demonstrating the overwhelming force of spiritual austerity.

top_scenes.scene_text: The divine cow Shabala stands beside sage Vasishtha as waves of warriors miraculously emerge from her body and charge across the battlefield.
Golden-skinned Shaka warriors in yellow armor surge across the earth like fire, overwhelming Vishwamitra’s chariots, elephants, and soldiers.
Sage Vasishtha calmly utters a single sacred sound while the hundred armed sons of Vishwamitra are instantly reduced to ashes before him.
